metadata.note: The Fonda, Johnstown & Gloversville - a 132-mile steam-and-electric system built on the glove industry of Fulton County. Incorporated 1867, its first train ran to Gloversville in late November 1870 over roughly 10 miles from Fonda, where it met the New York Central main line and the Erie Canal. The Gloversville & Northville pushed 16-17 miles north-east through Mayfield and Cranberry Creek to Northville (construction from October 1872, finished 1875-76), and the Gloversville & Broadalbin ran east to Vail Mills and Broadalbin. From the 1890s the FJ&G absorbed the local trolley companies - the Cayadutta Electric, the Gloversville Street Electric, the Mountain Lake Electric - and became a serious interurban: the Amsterdam Division came in 1901 and a double-track line was completed through Schenectady to Scotia in 1903, carrying glove-trade travellers to the NYC station at Schenectady. Northville and Sacandaga Park made it 'the Sacandaga Route of the Adirondacks', drawing vacationers from New York City, Albany and Syracuse. Three endings, all different: the Northville line was abandoned March 16, 1930 (last revenue train March 15) when the Conklingville dam drowned the Sacandaga valley to make Great Sacandaga Lake; the entire electric trolley operation shut down in 1938, the Schenectady route going on June 24, 1938 after its bridge was condemned that April 5, despite five high-speed Brill Bullet interurban cars bought in 1931-32 to win the traffic back; and a gas-electric doodlebug, car #340, kept a daily passenger run to Broadalbin going until the final mixed train ran Gloversville-Broadalbin on July 12, 1956. The company suspended operations in January 1974 after 107 years and its remains passed to Delaware Otsego Corporation.

geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API), routed by Dijkstra shortest path. The FJ&G is mapped under four different name tags that all had to be pulled together: 'Fonda, Gloversville & Johnstown Electric Railway', 'Fonda Johnstown and Gloversville', 'Fonda, Johnstown and Gloversville' and 'Fonda, Johnstown and Gloversville Rail Trail', plus the unnamed abandoned way carrying the Northville branch (OSM way 43932730) and the Mountain Lake ways (20082514, 43933180, 891753668).

Fonda-Johnstown-Gloversville main line: 13.9 km / 8.6 miles, 100% real-traced, no straight-line approximation. CAVEAT: OSM carries TWO closely parallel alignments in the Johnstown-Gloversville corridor - roughly 800 m apart on average - both under the 'Fonda, Gloversville & Johnstown Electric Railway' name, almost certainly the steam main line and the Cayadutta Electric street/trolley line. The trace follows the western one (mainly OSM way 43933183); the eastern chain (949247666 / 43933184) is not represented, and the interurban feature below is drawn over the same single alignment rather than over the trolley's actual street routing through Johnstown, Gloversville, Amsterdam and Schenectady.

Gloversville-Northville: 24.4 km / 15.2 miles, of which 4.4 km (18%) is a straight line from Gloversville north-east to Broadalbin Junction, where nothing is mapped. Beyond the junction the alignment is real-traced, but OSM way 43932730 is coarse (42 nodes over ~19 km) because most of this right of way has been under Great Sacandaga Lake since 1930. An earlier routing attempt that detoured north up the Mountain Lake spur and doubled back was rejected as implausible; the straight-line bridge preserves the correct east-north-east bearing that the mapped grade resumes at Broadalbin Junction.

Gloversville-Vail Mills-Broadalbin: 15.9 km / 9.9 miles, sharing the same 4.4 km straight-line bridge out of Gloversville (28% of this feature); east of Broadalbin Junction it is real-traced, largely as the FJ&G Rail Trail.

Gloversville-Johnstown-Amsterdam-Schenectady/Scotia interurban: 49.9 km / 31.0 miles, of which 3.1 km (6%) is straight-line bridging across gaps in the mapped grade, the largest between Hoffmans and the Scotia end.
Gloversville-Mountain Lake: 9.4 km / 5.9 miles, essentially all real-traced (0.1 km bridging).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact timetables for any era; every frequency below is estimated and unsourced. Sources also disagree on several dates, and where they do the value used is noted here: incorporation is given as January 17, 1867 by american-rails and June 16, 1867 by sacandagastation (1867 used); the first train as November 28 vs November 29, 1870 (1870 used); the Northville line's completion as summer 1876 vs 1875 (1876 used); the Brill Bullet purchase as 1931 vs 1932 (1931 used); the Cayadutta Electric's opening as 1893, with merger dates given variously as 1894, 1895 and 1902; and the Mountain Lake line's acquisition as 1903 vs 1904 (1903 used). Separately, the END of passenger service on the Fonda-Gloversville main line is NOT directly sourced - 1938 is used below because that is when the FJ&G shut its electric passenger operation down, but the only sourced post-1938 passenger date is the Broadalbin doodlebug running to July 12, 1956, so Fonda-Gloversville may have lasted longer than shown.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.interurban_audit: 2026-08-24: features on this layer that are inter-city electric railways were retagged mode='interurban' (previously 'streetcar' or 'intercity_rail') so the map can draw them distinctly from city streetcars and from steam roads. See CLAUDE.md Rule 7.
